text:
sam: Heads up — after rolling the new dynamic batching-window heuristic on staging we see weird idle gaps in the GPU kernel timeline. Captured nsys but attach failed on one node with permission/CUPTI errors. Anyone seen this?

maria: Can you paste the exact nsys command + error? Also which driver + nsys versions?

sam: Command I used:
```
nsys profile --trace=cuda,cupti -o /tmp/trace --sample=none --force ./run_inference.sh
```
On gpu-stg-05 the run aborts immediately. Error snippet in the log: `CUPTI initialization failed: CUPTI_ERROR_INVALID_DEVICE` (and sometimes 'permission denied'). Node driver: 535.54. Container runtime: dockerd v24 + runc. nsys: 2023.4.1.

leo: Sounds like a container attach/ptrace/seccomp issue. We've had cases where nsys can't open /proc/<pid>/mem or ptrace is blocked. Check perf_event_paranoid and whether debugfs is mounted. :thinking_face: 

jen: Also worth noting — after the batching change our KV cache miss rate spiked. That produced many shorter kernels (200-400us) which interact badly with sampling and timeline clarity. But the attach failure on that node looks separate.

sam: On healthy nodes the timeline shows lots of short kernels with 120-300us gaps. On the failing node the app runs fine but nsys immediately fails. Full attach log: 
```
CUPTI failed to connect to process 23456: CUPTI_ERROR_INVALID_PARAMETER (0x...)
nsys: error: failed to start profiling: CUPTI initialization failed
```

maria: Which kernel + nvidia modules are loaded? Is the NVIDIA container toolkit installed correctly? Try running nsys from the host and attach to the container PID, and try nsys 2024.1 vs 2023.4 — there are CUPTI API changes that sometimes mismatch driver builds.

leo: Quick repro steps I recommend: try `nsys profile --trace=cuda,cpu --nvtx ./app` (no cupti) and see if it succeeds. If it does, then the issue is strictly CUPTI-level. Check dmesg for 'cupti' or 'permission' messages too.

sam: Tried host attach; same failure. SELinux is permissive on the node. Runtime seccomp profile is basically default. One difference: failing node runs kernel 6.3 while the healthy ones are 5.15. Driver 535 on 6.3 might trigger a scheduling regression (NV folks hinted at split-kernel behavior with older driver combos) — could explain both timing oddities and attach instability.

jen: From perf perspective the batching heuristic caused less coalescing so more small kernels; that increases scheduling overhead. If driver+kernel combo stalls on small launches, it looks like a perf regression. Can we revert the heuristic to fixed-window for a quick A/B? :eyes: 

maria: Workarounds we've used: (1) run nsys on the host and `--attach=PID` with CAP_SYS_PTRACE; (2) grant the container CAP_SYS_PTRACE or run with `--security-opt seccomp=unconfined` for trace runs; (3) pin nsys to an older minor that matches the driver (or try the newer nsys that bundles a different CUPTI). Also try `nsys profile --capture-range=nvtx --attach=23456` from host as a diagnostic.

sam: I'll try CAP_SYS_PTRACE and then roll back the batching-window change to observe KV cache hit patterns. I also want to capture a .qdrep + perfetto system trace if workarounds fail.

ops-bot: Incident created: PERF-2026-87 for staging GPU traces. Assignee: leo. :white_check_mark: 

leo: Assigned. If we confirm a driver bug we'll open an NVIDIA ticket and include the nsys .qdrep, the host kernel timeline (perfetto), and dmesg/cuipti logs. Also planning to run a CUDA-only nsys profile and a perfetto capture to correlate cpu<->gpu gaps.

sam: One more note — I saw `cuptiActivityEnqueueBuffer` warnings in dmesg when nsys tried to collect on that node; looks like a mmap/permission mapping issue. I'll attach logs to the incident after the CAP_SYS_PTRACE run.

jen: Great. If reverting the heuristic restores KV cache hit rates and reduces scheduling pressure that will isolate the regression to the batching change + driver/kernel combo. Thanks team.
